edited_statements.before: Her only test of probable truth is what works best in the way of leading us, what fits every part of life best and combines with the collectivity of experience's demands, nothing being omitted.
edited_statements.after: Pragmatism's only test of probable truth is what works best in the way of leading us, what fits every part of life best and combines with the collectivity of experience's demands, nothing being omitted.
edited_statements.why: Opened the note on 'Her', whose referent (pragmatism) stayed in the previous note; replaced with the source's own name 'Pragmatism' (name span with its own footnote, 's added for the possessive).

hard_calls: Statements 3-6 ("Surely you must admit this...", "But in this world...") refer back to the two definitional sentences, so they stay merged with them in the first note.

The 'What would be better for us to believe' note runs about 218 words: 'Pragmatism says no' and 'Probably you also agree' answer the preceding question and could not be split off without edits, so the whole paragraph stays together.
The Absolute note holds nine statements as one worked example (belief must run the gauntlet, then is given up); splitting it would strand 'it' and 'them' references.
The 'democratic she' closing paragraph is kept with the 'only test' note rather than the God-search note to keep both near 120-170 words and avoid a second name-span edit.
The Absolute-restriction note could be merged into the Absolute note, but merged it would run about 240 words, so it stays separate.
